sections.title: The Reign of Azariah (Uzziah)
observations: Azariah, also known as Uzziah, became king of Judah at a young age and reigned for 52 years. His reign is noted for both his accomplishments and his failures. He started well, seeking the Lord and following the example of his father, Amaziah.

Under Azariah's leadership, Judah experienced military success and economic prosperity. He fortified Jerusalem and expanded the kingdom's borders, which reflects God's blessing on his reign as long as he remained faithful.

sections.title: The Downfall of Azariah
observations: Despite his initial faithfulness, Azariah's pride led to his downfall. He attempted to burn incense in the temple, an act reserved for the priests. This act of disobedience resulted in God striking him with leprosy, demonstrating that even a king is not above God's law.
Azariah's leprosy forced him to live in isolation, and his son Jotham governed in his place. This serves as a reminder of the consequences of pride and disobedience to God's commands.

sections.title: The Reigns of Other Kings
observations: The chapter also details the reigns of several other kings of Israel, including Zechariah, Shallum, Menahem, and Pekahiah. Each of these kings had a brief and tumultuous reign, often marked by violence and idolatry.
The mention of these kings highlights the instability in Israel during this period, contrasting with the more stable reign of Azariah in Judah.

sections.title: The Rise of Pekah
observations: Pekah, one of the last kings of Israel, is noted for his military alliances and conflicts with Judah. His reign is characterized by further decline in faithfulness to God, leading to eventual judgment.
The chapter concludes with the mention of the Assyrian threat, foreshadowing the impending judgment on Israel due to their unfaithfulness.

importantVerses.commentary: The Lord struck the king, so that he was a leper to the day of his death. This verse emphasizes the seriousness of Azariah's sin and the immediate consequences of his actions.
This verse highlights the fulfillment of God's judgment against Israel, as Pekah's reign leads to further decline and eventual destruction.

questions: What can we learn from Azariah's initial faithfulness and subsequent downfall?
How does the instability of Israel's kings reflect the nation's spiritual condition?
What lessons can be drawn from the consequences of pride and disobedience in leadership?
